success_criteria:
    - "READ THE TRIAGE NOTES FIRST. Run `bd show` on ethos-bfml, ethos-hy40, ethos-kcbv, ethos-e05k, ethos-jw1z. Each carries a triage note dated 2026-09-10 written after verifying the bead against 4.18.0 source. TWO of them are corrected by those notes — build to the note, not the original text."
    - "THE CENTRAL FINDING: ethos-bfml and ethos-hy40 are ONE defect, not two. bfml reports three PASSes on a repo with no hooks; hy40 is the same thing from the commit-msg side. Its filed premise ('doctor checks only the seal hook') is FALSE as of 4.18.0 — trailerHookSpec exists and CheckHookCurrency runs over both. Fix them together."
    - "DO NOT make CheckHookCurrency fail on an absent section. Its PASS-on-absence is deliberate and DOCUMENTED in its own doc comment ('a section that doesn't exist is not this check's concern'), and it is correct for a CURRENCY check — a dormant repo must not be told its absent hooks are stale. Inverting that breaks the dormant case. The real gap is PRESENCE, not currency: seal presence when enabled IS checked (the 'Audit seal hook' check reads the enabled marker); trailer presence when enabled is NOT checked at all; and nothing composes 'this repo is enabled AND a required hook is missing' into a failure. Fix the gap, not the semantic."
    - "ethos-kcbv SHOULD LAND FIRST and the ordering is the point. hasActiveSealCall (internal/doctor/doctor.go:372) is still a lexical scan of shell source — SplitKeepEnds + HeredocMask + stripInlineComment + a sealInvocation regex — and all four documented patch rounds are visible in that code. A stop-loss was declared during v4.1.1: the next lexical corner converts it to execution-based verification. Building the new presence check on top of the current scanner adds a fifth consumer to the thing that keeps breaking. Convert it first, then build presence on the converted detector. If you conclude execution-based verification is infeasible here, STOP and report why with evidence rather than quietly adding a fifth lexical patch."
    - "ethos-e05k: add a doctor check flagging code archetypes (implement, test) whose DEPLOYED YAML lacks require_delegated_worker. The invariant is data-driven from deployed archetype files, so an operator who upgrades the binary without re-running `ethos seed` silently gets ZERO enforcement, and a stale repo-local archetype shadows an updated global one. Verified 2026-09-10: no such check exists in internal/doctor/. Check both layers, and make the detail name which layer is stale."
    - "ethos-jw1z: the orphaned-agent FAIL detail (internal/doctor/doctor.go:229) reads 'orphaned agent files (not on any team)', which sounds like data corruption. The common real cause is stale generated files left over from a team-scope change. Distinguish the two so the operator learns what to DO — a stale generated file is safe to delete; a genuine orphan is not. Do not guess the classification; derive it from something checkable."
    - "EVERY new or changed check needs a test that is verified FAILING against pre-fix code before the fix lands. State which you confirmed red and paste the pre-fix output. This is not boilerplate on this bead: the defect being fixed IS a check that reports success without verifying, and five tests on the immediately preceding branch were found guarding their own fixture rather than their stated property. A test for a health check that has never been observed failing is the exact bug you are fixing, one level up."
    - "make check green before EVERY commit, race detector included. No suppressions."
    - "GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./... must exit 0."
    - "Run the detached test gate before reporting and give BOTH the ok count AND the FAIL count — a zero FAIL count alone cannot distinguish nothing-failed from nothing-ran."
    - "DESIGN.md ADR for the presence-vs-currency decision and for the execution-based conversion, including rejected alternatives. State explicitly what the new checks do NOT cover — an ADR that overstates what it closes is a defect on this repo; three defects survived a full review round on the last branch because an earlier draft understated its residuals."
    - "CHANGELOG under [Unreleased]. Doctor output is user-facing: new checks and changed detail text are Added/Changed, not Fixed. The previous release shipped two new capabilities miscategorized under Fixed and needed a follow-up PR to correct the release notes."
    - "Commit incrementally — one commit per logical step. Each commit passes make check. Do not accumulate more than 30 minutes of uncommitted changes."
    - "Do NOT push. Report and the leader pushes."
budget:
    rounds: 3
    reflection_after_each: true
context: |
    Cluster 3 of the ethos bug triage: doctor / health-check correctness.
    Five beads, all verified real against 4.18.0 source on 2026-09-10
    before this contract was written.

    The unifying theme, and the reason this cluster was picked next: every
    one of these is a check that reports success without having verified
    the thing it claims to check, or that reports a fact without the
    context needed to act on it. That is the same defect class the last two
    clusters kept producing — a release phase validating the file it had
    just written, five tests guarding their own fixtures, a website check
    blind to whether the deploy shipped. Here it is in the tool operators
    run specifically to learn whether their install is sound, which makes
    it the most expensive instance of it.

    Concrete evidence this matters, from 2026-09-08: a stale install URL
    downgraded the operator's binary and rewrote this repo's git hooks to
    an older build. Doctor's currency check DID notice — the fingerprint
    moved. So the machinery half-works, which is precisely why the false
    PASS on absence is worth fixing rather than dismissing.

    Read the triage notes on the beads before the original text. Two
    filings are corrected there: hy40's premise is stale, and bfml's root
    cause is narrower than its title.

Work in <repo> on branch `fix/doctor-health-checks` (already created, clean, based on main at the v4.18.0 release). Do NOT create or switch worktrees or branches.

Each carries a note dated 2026-09-10 written after I verified it against 4.18.0 source. **Two filings are corrected there.** `ethos-hy40` says "doctor checks only the seal hook" — that is FALSE now; `trailerHookSpec` exists and `CheckHookCurrency` runs over both. Building to the filed text would produce the wrong fix.

2. **`bfml` and `hy40` are one defect.** Three PASSes on a repo with no hooks, and the commit-msg side of the same gap. Fix together.

3. **Do not make `CheckHookCurrency` fail on absence.** That PASS is deliberate and documented in its own doc comment, and correct for a *currency* check — a dormant repo must not be told its absent hooks are stale. The gap is PRESENCE: seal presence when enabled is checked, trailer presence is not, and nothing composes "enabled AND missing" into a failure.

4. **Convert `hasActiveSealCall` to execution-based verification first (`ethos-kcbv`), then build presence on the converted detector.** It is still lexical — `SplitKeepEnds` + `HeredocMask` + `stripInlineComment` + regex — with four documented patch rounds visible in the code, and a stop-loss already declared. Adding a fifth consumer to it is building on the thing that keeps breaking. If you conclude execution-based verification is genuinely infeasible here, STOP and report why with evidence rather than adding a fifth lexical patch.

**On tests, specifically for this bead.** Every new or changed check needs a test confirmed FAILING against pre-fix code, with the pre-fix output pasted. **Before you commit, state what your change makes worse, if anything.** If the honest answer is "nothing," say what you checked to conclude that. A limitation disclosed in your report but not in the code comment is functionally undisclosed — that exact miss cost a round on the last branch.
